_: xcode — the xcodebuild/xcrun/swiftlint surface of an iOS project.
scope   compile, test and inspect. Anything that signs, uploads or changes
the machine's toolchain is not here: `archive`/`-exportArchive`,
not left at ask, because none of them is a step in reading or
actions {{xcode_action}} is the verb list an agent needs to prove a change:
clean. `clean build-for-testing` is a common one-command spelling,
so a leading `clean` is allowed in front of another verb.
simctl  read-only subcommands only. `simctl erase` and `simctl delete`
throw away a simulator and its state — a delete, so it is denied.
lint    swiftlint is invoked by a vendored path in the repo, set in
outside the Edit tool and is left to ask, so the diff a human sees
is the diff the agent made.
scripts one reviewed CI entry point by exact name: BuildScripts/ci_xcodebuild.sh.
Rename it in your project's rules.json if yours is spelled differently.

deny.reason: archiving and exporting an .ipa is a release step, not a build check
that flag lets the build mutate signing assets on the developer account
erasing or deleting a simulator throws away state a failing test run may be the only record of
deny.note: A deny and not a recompose, for the same reason as node.cache-clean: there is no tidier spelling of throwing something away. `simctl shutdown` and `simctl boot` are not here — they change nothing on disk, so they fall through to ask.

deny.reason: switching the active toolchain changes the machine, not the project

allow.note: the verb may be preceded by `clean`, which is how a from-scratch test build is usually spelled
`--fix` is excluded by lookahead, not merely absent from the flag list: the trailing path argument would otherwise swallow it. It edits source outside the Edit tool, so it asks.

cases: xcodebuild clean build-for-testing -project App.xcodeproj -scheme App -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,OS=26.1,name=iPhone 17 Pro"
